title: heap-use-after-free in findElementWithHash
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: detachFunc frees the auxiliary btree and schema in attach.c while a TEMP TRIGGER in aDb[1] keeps pTabSchema pointing at it, and sqlite3DropTriggerPtr -> tableOfTrigger reads pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash in trigger.c. Fixed upstream in 3.30.0
object: the auxiliary database's Schema, and the table hash inside it
lifetime_ender: DETACH frees the auxiliary btree and schema while a temp trigger still points at them
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Built in the coreT group (-USQLITE_OMIT_TEMPDB): without a temp database the trigger has nowhere to survive

fault_sites_why: The stale access is the first load from the freed auxiliary schema: sqlite3DropTriggerPtr calls tableOfTrigger, which only forms the address &pTrigger->pTabSchema->tblHash, and sqlite3HashFind passes it on; the first load is pH->ht in findElementWithHash. Host ASan agrees -- its access stack is findElementWithHash <- sqlite3HashFind <- tableOfTrigger <- sqlite3DropTriggerPtr, 24 bytes inside a 120-byte region freed by sqlite3DbFreeNN <- sqlite3BtreeClose (results/2026-10-11-host-asan). NARROWED 2026-10-15, from [sqlite3DropTriggerPtr, tableOfTrigger, sqlite3HashFind, findElementWithHash] to this one: the other three are the call chain, and listing them made any fault along it count as a catch, including the NULL dereference this defect causes downstream. Probe site 43 measures the difference -- on stock memsys5, natively and on virtual Capstone and CheriBSD purecap alike, the stale load SUCCEEDS (kind=UAF witnessed, no fault) and returns ht=0 htsize=0 count=0 first=0, so findElementWithHash returns &nullElement, sqlite3HashFind returns NULL, and sqlite3DropTriggerPtr then dereferences that NULL (its assert(pTable) is compiled out by NDEBUG). Those arms fault at address 0x0 in sqlite3DropTriggerPtr, and CheriBSD reports si_code=2, PROT_CHERI_TAG, an untagged dereference -- the consequence of the defect, not a rejection of the invalid access.
